subject: Dedicated capacity: burst-sizing & autoscale policy for Atlas Health deal
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Atlas Health Infrastructure <infra@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod peaks during billing window — Dedicated sizing question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We ran a week of load tests against the dedicated preview and saw a few concerning spikes during our billing ingestion window (1:45–2:15am PT) that pushed token throughput ~2.8x baseline for short bursts (~4–7 minutes). Logs attached (Atlas_PROD_spike_logs.csv).

Before we sign the committed capacity contract, the infra team needs to understand Redwood's burst/overprovisioning behavior and how autoscale would handle these short, sharp spikes without blowing our cost estimates. Specifically:
- Can Dedicated be configured to ramp up GPUs for 5–10 minute bursts above the reserved pool?
- Is there a hard cap on instantaneous vGPU allocation per customer?
- How does billing work for burst capacity — per-minute, per-second, or full-hour increments?

We're aiming for predictable economics. If you can map a recommended burst policy to our test logs, that would help us finalize the internal purchase order. Looping in infra (infra@atlashealth.com).

Thanks,
Maya Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maya Rao <maya@atlashealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod peaks during billing window — Dedicated sizing question

Maya — thanks for the logs, this is exactly the kind of signal we wanted before finalizing the commitment. Quick answers up front:
- Yes, Dedicated supports short-duration burst capacity that can be scoped per-contract; we typically surface it as a % of reserved pool (e.g., +50% burst for 10 mins) or an absolute GPU count.
- There is a soft instantaneous limit tied to available cluster capacity and customer tier; we enforce fallbacks when capacity is constrained.
- Billing for burst capacity on Hosted Dedicated is prorated to the minute (with a 1-minute granularity) — we provide metered usage in Console. For private/on-prem customers billing is based on contracted terms.

I've looped in Jordan (SE) and Evelyn (Infra) to propose a policy that maps to your spike patterns. We're prepping a sample autoscale policy and a short SLA addendum to make economics explicit.

Action: Jordan and Evelyn, can you review the attached test logs and propose a burst policy (minutes, GPU delta, throttle behaviour) that keeps median latency under 200ms during spikes and caps cost uplift to ~20% over baseline?

I can pull an initial draft for the PO after we agree the policy.

— Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Maya Rao <maya@atlashealth.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod peaks during billing window — Dedicated sizing question

Maya / Karthik — I dug into the CSV you sent. Notes:
- The spikes are short and repeatable (~5–7 minutes), with peak token/sec ~2.6–3x baseline; tail latency during peaks climbs to ~420ms on the smaller instances.
- For Atlas's workload shape (many short chats, some long-context batched jobs), we recommend a hybrid policy: keep baseline reserved pool sized for 95th percentile of normal hours, then enable a 50% burst pool with 10-minute max hold and a 2-minute cooldown.
- Autoscaler knobs: ramp rate (GPUs/min) = 4 GPUs/min, max simultaneous scale steps = 2, and pre-warm affinity for KV-cache warmup on prefetched model shards.

I'm attaching a proposed_autoscale_policy.yaml with the concrete values and a short runbook for expected billing impact under the CSV trace (simulated). If that shape looks good, Evelyn can speak to the cluster-level constraints and availability.

Jordan Blake
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_autoscale_policy.yaml
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Rao <maya@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod peaks during billing window — Dedicated sizing question

Team / Maya — a few infra constraints and recommendations from our side:
- Cluster availability: for the March window our US clusters show sufficient spare capacity, but we always recommend a contractual burst guardrail (absolute GPU cap) in case regional pressure increases. For Atlas I suggest: reserved=40 GPUs, burst cap=+20 GPUs (50% bump), burst max duration=10 mins.
- Warmup: to keep latency predictable we recommend 30s pre-warm for KV caches; Jordan's pre-warm affinity is important.
- Billing note: minute-level metering is applied; daily rollups are visible in Console and we'll include a pre-signing cost simulation PDF in the SLA-addendum-draft.pdf.

I've attached an SLA addendum draft that enumerates the burst guarantees, metering, and fallback policy. Two operational caveats: 1) if the burst pool is exhausted we will automatically gate to the highest-compatible model (lower-capacity variant) and 2) we provide a webhook/event stream with burst utilization metrics so Atlas can ingest and alert.

If you want, we can add an explicit clause for a one-time credit cap if overspend exceeds a threshold in the first 90 days while traffic patterns stabilize.

— Evelyn
Sr. Infra PM, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA-addendum-draft.pdf
From: Maya Rao <maya@atlashealth.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 17:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod peaks during billing window — Dedicated sizing question

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with our procurement ask. A few confirmations from Atlas infra:
- We're comfortable with reserved=40 GPUs and a documented +20 GPU burst cap for 10 minutes.
- We want the one-time credit cap for the first 60 days (procurement will discuss exact $ cap). Please add that to the SLA draft.
- Can you add a short sample of the Console alert webhook payload so we can wire it to PagerDuty?

Once the SLA addendum includes the credit clause and the HubSpot/DocuSign links are ready, procurement is prepared to sign the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Maya
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas Health
